name: aziridine
label: mol:c-C2H4NH
latex_body: \citet{Dickens:2001:643} reported the tentative detection of the $J_{K_a,K_c} = 5_{5,0}\rightarrow4_{4,1}$ transition of \ce{c-C2H4NH}, also known as ethylenimine, at 226~GHz toward Sgr B2, G34.3+0.2, G10.47+0.03, and G327.3-0.6 in observations made with the SEST 15-m, NRAO 12-m, and NASA Deep Space Network 70-m telescopes.  The laboratory data were reported by \citet{Thorwirth:2000:323,Thorwirth:2000:116,Tolles:1965:2253}.

name: acetylide anion
label: mol:C2H-
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:2008:L83} suggest that an unidentified line at 83.278\,GHz, classified as U83278, in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216 may be due to the $J = 1\rightarrow0$ transition of \ce{C2H-}.  Although they list no source for their line frequency, it presumably is derived from the work of \citet{Brunken:2007:L33} and \citet{Amano:2008:244305}.

name: iron monoxide
label: mol:FeO
latex_body: \citet{Walmsley:2002:L109} identified an absorption feature in IRAM 30-m observations of Sgr B2 at 153~GHz that they tentatively assign to the $J = 5\rightarrow4$, $\Omega = 4$ transition of FeO, based on the laboratory work of \citet{Allen:1996:130}.  Later, \citet{Furuya:2003:L21} used the Nobeyama Millimeter Array to confirm the detection of this line, but no additional transitions were observed.  Most recently, \citet{Decin:2018:113} reported a tentative detection of the $11\rightarrow10$, $\Omega = 4$ transition in ALMA observations of R Dor at 337~GHz.

name: glycine
label: mol:NH2CH2COOH
latex_body: \citet{Kuan:2003:848} reported a detection of 27 lines of \ce{NH2CH2COOH} in observations toward Orion, Sgr B2, and W51 using the NRAO 12-m telescope.  Each source contained 13--16 of the 27 features; three features were seen in common between the sources.  The frequencies were obtained from the rotational constants measured and reported in \citet{Suenram:1980:7180} and \citet{Lovas:1995:L201}.  The detection was later disputed by \citet{Snyder:2005:914}, who claimed to have identified a number of issues with the analysis.  Notably, \citet{Snyder:2005:914} argue that the frequency predictions used by \citet{Kuan:2003:848} were extrapolated too far above the measured laboratory transitions.  \citet{Snyder:2005:914} used laboratory frequencies from \citet{Ilyushin:2005:15} that covered the observed frequency range, and examined archival NRAO 12-m and SEST 15-m observations of Orion, Sgr B2, and W51.  They report a number of ``missing'' transitions of \ce{NH2CH2COOH} that they predicted should have been strongly detected, if the detection of \citet{Kuan:2003:848} held.  Subsequent searches by \citet{Jones:2007:579}, \citet{Cunningham:2007:1201}, and \citet{Belloche:2008:179} using both interferometers and single-dish facilities failed to detect \ce{NH2CH2COOH}, and set upper limits to the column density lower than that claimed in the detection of \citet{Kuan:2003:848} (see \citealt{Belloche:2008:179} \S4.4 for a detailed discussion).

name: protonated cyanodiacetylene cation
label: mol:HC5NH+
latex_body: \citet{Marcelino:2020:L6} report a tentative detection of \ce{HC5NH+} in Yebes 40-m observations of TMC-1.  They identify a series of eight harmonically spaced lines in the data corresponding to a rotational constant $B$ = 1295.8158\,MHz.  Based on quantum chemical calculations, they suggest either \ce{HC5NH+} or \ce{NC4NH+} as the potential carrier, eventually proposing \ce{HC5NH+} as the more likely.

name: cyanophosphaethyne
label: mol:NCCP
latex_body: \citet{Agundez:2014:A45} reported the tentative detection of \ce{NCCP} in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216.  They identified and tentatively assigned three signals in their spectra to the $J = 15\rightarrow14$, $16\rightarrow15$, and $18\rightarrow17$ transitions of \ce{NCCP} at 81, 87, and 97~GHz, respectively, based on the laboratory work of \citet{Bizzocchi:2001:110}.
